mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for three consecutive months, market expectations of future rate cuts increase, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1-year average(FEDFUNDS) for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in such periods are not statistically higher than in non-cut regimes (t-test p > 0.05), or the Fed signals a reversal before the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) simultaneously reduces labor-market tightness and boosts household spending, jointly pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.2×(PAYEMS lag 1 month) AND HOUST > 0.15×(HOUST lag 1 month)
regime_hint: Labor market loosening with rising consumer sentiment
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20-day windows where both proxies meet the trigger, or the correlation falls below 0.7 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2 percentage points signals weakening supply-side constraints, prompting investors to anticipate higher future demand and bid up equity valuations, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO lag 1 month by > 2.0 percentage points for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns remain flat or negative in such events, or the effect is not statistically significant (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in a month, markets anticipate a policy response that may slow future rate hikes, lowering real discount rates and supporting equity valuations, resulting in a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day forward return in such inflation spikes, or the effect is short-lived (< 1 month).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, prompting the Fed to raise rates, which compresses equity discount rates and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0 + 0.1×(UNRATE lag 1 month) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day or 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in such regimes (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both job openings (PAYEMS) and unemployment (UNRATE) exceeding 5% and 0.5 percentage points, respectively, indicate a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports consumer spending, driving a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < PAYEMS lag 1 month by > 5.0% AND UNRATE < UNRATE lag 1 month by > 0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: No significant positive return in triggered windows, or interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; therefore, this hypothesis is omitted) would indicate consumer weakness, but since it cannot be measured with the given proxies, this slot is reserved for a regime-conditional alternative: In a regime of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5), a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% suggests supply-side shock, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.5 AND INDPRO < INDPRO lag 1 month by > 3.0 percentage points
failure_condition: No negative return in such events, or the interaction is not robust to out-of-sample splits.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, signaling persistent tightening, investors anticipate higher future rates, which increases discounting of future cash flows and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days in a non-recessionary regime.
failure_condition: No significant negative return in such windows, or the effect is only observed during recessionary episodes.
